content: During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. It may be part of a treatment plan to reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. However, it is not known if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is important to maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Some products, such as orlistat, may interact with this medication. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. Before starting this medication and during its use, laboratory and medical tests (such as liver function tests, viral load, and T-cell counts) should be conducted. It is essential to keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase this effect. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, if you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. For any questions or concerns about side effects, U.S. residents should contact their doctor, and Canadian residents should do the same.
